notes: Seed list for the EUR-Lex/CELLAR connector. The EU is treated as a jurisdiction in its own right. CJEU judgments exist in all official languages; the connector fetches English where available and the procedural language otherwise, so this list carries EN plus the three most common procedural languages for pesticide cases. Add further language sections as the corpus demands. Instrument numbers (1107/2009, 528/2012) are the highest-precision signals in this jurisdiction and are language-independent. Revision 1.0.1 (issue #20): DDT split out of en-paraquat into its own case-sensitive word term, mirroring nl-ddt, so acronyms and prose words never share a term. Revision 1.0.2: the exception notes claimed these authority names are always capitalised so the exposure is theoretical. Measurement refuted that - the acronym is case-sensitive too, so efsa, Efsa, nvwa and echa all score 0. Notes now point at the README, which records the measured cost. No term, weight or threshold changed. Revision 1.1.0 (issue #55): scoring.review_band added, set to 3. It flags, and does not reject: a passing case scoring in [3, 6) is ingested and published as normal and additionally queued for a content manager. The number is this corpus own: in the first EU dry run the false positives were concentrated immediately above min_score while the top band was almost entirely genuine, so the population that raising min_score would have discarded is reviewed instead. That trade was declined; see core document 2.7 for the distribution and the figures, and issue #8 for the run itself. Figures are not restated here on purpose (issue #67): a derived number copied into a second artefact is a place to drift, and this note previously carried a miscounted one. No term, weight or threshold changed. Revision 1.2.0: the active substances of the Annex to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 540/2011 are now carried in full - 486 new weight-3 active_substance terms, on top of the fourteen this list already had. They were extracted from the English text of every consolidated version of that regulation published between 2011 and 2026, not only the current one, because a substance whose approval was not renewed is deleted from the Annex while remaining exactly what historic and liability litigation is about. Parts A to E are all included: approved, basic, low-risk, candidates for substitution, and everything since withdrawn. The literals are the ISO common names the Annex prints, in English only; national-language spellings belong in the national lists. A single-token name is matched on word boundaries unless it is at least ten characters long, where substring also catches compounds and inflections; a multi-word name is matched as a phrase; a micro-organism is carried as its genus and species, and a virus by its name, since a strain designation is not what a judgment prints. Sixty-six of these names are also ordinary English words or commodities - beer, vinegar, sulphur, urea, pepper, whey - and would each qualify a customs or agricultural judgment on their own, so they carry requires=[en-pesticide]: they still report their match, but only contribute weight in a document that also names a pesticide. No existing term, weight, threshold or band changed. Revision 1.3.0: metam leaves en-fipronil and becomes a term of its own matched on word boundaries. match is a property of a term and all of its aliases, so the five-character ISO name inherited the substring mode fipronil can carry and the shorter name cannot. Dutch is one of this list's languages, and in 150,000 Dutch judgments the fragment appears in 217 documents of which 214 hold metamfetamine, metamorfose or trometamol rather than the substance; at weight 3 each of those would have been selected on the fragment alone. As a whole word it still finds metam, metam-sodium and metam natrium. Adding a term can raise the score of a document naming both metam and fipronil, so this is a minor bump; no other term, weight, threshold or band changed.

terms.note: A term of its own because match is a property of the term and all of its aliases: as an alias of en-fipronil it inherited substring, and five characters reaches inside unrelated words. In 150,000 Dutch judgments - Dutch is one of this list's languages - 214 of the 217 documents holding the fragment held it inside metamfetamine, metamorfose or trometamol, and three held the substance. Matched as a whole word it still finds metam-sodium and metam natrium.
Acronym, kept as its own case-sensitive term so it is not matched as a substring inside unrelated tokens. Mirrors nl-ddt.
